name: WinPEAP
description: WinPEAP is a WinPE-based workflow to transition devices to Entra Joined and auto-enroll them into Intune via Windows Autopilot. It uses OSDCloud to build a customized WinPE ISO, injects the 4kAutopilotHashUpload.ps1 script and oa3tool-based hardware hash capture, and uploads the Autopilot hash to Intune during WinPE. Automation spans OS deployment, driver injection, hash registration, and enrollment, with support for user-driven Autopilot profiles and VM testing considerations.
author: Beau LaWalt

securityCheck.aiSummary: Overall assessment: The WinPEAP/OSDCloud automation appears to be a legitimate enterprise deployment tool leveraging Microsoft Graph and Autopilot. The primary security concern is the dynamic remote code loading in bootstrap.ps1 (remote script download and execution), which introduces risk if the source can be tampered with. Additional concerns include sensitive data handling (hardware hash) stored locally, secrets exposure risks through config-stored AppSecret, and logging that could capture sensitive data. Recommendations include: signing and pinning remote scripts or converting to signed modules, implementing integrity checks (hash/signature) for downloaded code, securing config.json and secrets (prefer vault/certificate-based auth), encrypting or securely handling hardware hashes, and limiting/log redacting transcript output. If remote script delivery must be retained, consider a hardened workflow with code signing, delivery manifests, and reduced trust in external sources.
